This verb and addressee shape are why the verse sits in the 49-verse any-form word-event count and not the 48-verse first-person family (sweep: verses containing the word-event phrase in any form, 49; the 48 excludes this one verse by predicate). It is weighed here as a real onset in its own right, not folded into or discounted against the vision that follows. The same verse also carries וַתְּהִ֥י עָלָ֛יו שָׁ֖ם יַד יְהוָֽה, the hand-of-YHWH construct that opens the book's first vision (one of 7 verses carrying the construct). Close: the scene runs unbroken to oshb:Ezek.1.28, מַרְאֵ֖ה דְּמ֣וּת כְּבוֹד יְהוָ֑ה וָֽאֶרְאֶה֙ וָאֶפֹּ֣ל עַל פָּנַ֔י וָאֶשְׁמַ֖ע ק֥וֹל מְדַבֵּֽר, glossed by the WEB as “This was the appearance of the likeness of Yahweh’s glory. When I saw it, I fell on my face, and I heard a voice of one that spoke” (web:Ezek.1.28). No word-event, messenger, recognition or utterance formula interrupts 1:4-1:27 (the transport-verb and 'he said to me' sweeps that mark scene changes elsewhere in the book's visions do not begin until chapter 8), so the throne-theophany carries no formula-marked internal seam; the samekh recorded after 1:28 and the fresh 'he said to me' that opens oshb:Ezek.2.1 together mark the vision/commission seam on the FAR side of this unit; the onset evidence at oshb:Ezek.2.1 is weighed there.

live_prose.boundary_rationale: Onset side: the hard-seam dateline at oshb:Ezek.29.1 (year 10, month 10, day 12) uses the perfect hayah word-event form, immediately followed by the set-your-face address to Pharaoh at oshb:Ezek.29.2 and the messenger formula opening the verdict speech at oshb:Ezek.29.3 (the great-monster-in-his-rivers charge). Close side: the strict recognition formula at oshb:Ezek.29.9a closes the crocodile-verdict unit; the same verse continues with a causal clause the WEB itself paragraphs mid-verse (web:Ezek.29.9), and oshb:Ezek.29.10 opens a fresh against-you verdict cycle restating the same charge -- an onset/close collision at 29:9 -> 29:10 -- so the row seam sits at the verse boundary after 29:9, not inside it.
live_prose.strongest_rejected_alternative: Three alternatives are weighed. (1) Ending the row at 29:6, where an extended (non-strict) recognition-type close occurs; rejected because 29:7 continues the same staff-of-reed image with no intervening onset, and because this chapter's own onset/close collision pattern places the true seam after 29:9, not 29:6. Two further readings are weighed. (2) Cutting at 29:7/29:8 - the alternative the paragraph layer proposes, and the witness's sectioning is disclosed for it: MEASURED, this witness places a SAMEKH (setumah, closed section, single-witness) after MT 29:7, recorded on the verse it follows, and that verse additionally carries one ketiv/qere pair, already disclosed in this row. What the rival's near face carries: MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, MT 29:8 opens on the long-form messenger formula after a therefore-particle (oshb:Ezek.29.8), and with it a grammatical addressee shift - MT 29:7 addresses a masculine singular and MT 29:8 a feminine singular (oshb:Ezek.29.7, oshb:Ezek.29.8), that is, from Pharaoh to the land. Whether it is licensed: a messenger formula cuts as a sub-onset when its addressee differs from the one before or when the preceding verse ends on a close-role formula, and the first of those IS satisfied by that addressee change, so this rival is licensed and two-faced and is not dismissed. Its far face is nevertheless thin: MT 29:7 ends with no close-role formula, so the second would fail there and only the SAMEKH stands. The stated ground on which this row holds: the crocodile verdict's own refrain is the recognition formula at MT 29:9, and MT 29:10 restates the same charge as a fresh against-you cycle (oshb:Ezek.29.10); since a licensed text signal takes precedence over a section mark, the SAMEKH after MT 29:7 is weak corroboration, disclosed FOR this rival and not for this row. A licensed two-faced rival held on stated grounds leaves the boundary evidence at medium, where this row's grade sits. (3) Tiling MT 29:1-29:16 as ONE row, with the mid-verse WEB paragraph at 29:9 and the forty-years turn at 29:13 falling inside it. What supports it: MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, no dateline and no word-event formula stands anywhere between MT 29:1 and the next dateline at MT 29:17; MEASURED in this witness, the only marks inside that stretch follow MT 29:7 and MT 29:12 (single witness), and NO mark stands on MT 29:9. And this row's own close has the weak mid-verse shape: MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, the recognition formula in MT 29:9 ends at the etnachta and an INDEPENDENT causal clause with a finite verb fills the rest of the verse (oshb:Ezek.29.9) - unlike MT 29:6, whose words after its own recognition clause are a causal phrase built on an infinitive construct (oshb:Ezek.29.6), a dependent completion that grades as an ordinary licensed near-face signal rather than the weak mid-verse shape. The stated ground on which this row holds: MT 29:10 opens a fresh against-you verdict cycle restating the charge, so the collision is resolved at the verse boundary after 29:9. The weakness of the 29:9 close and the case for a single 29:1-16 row are disclosed rather than argued away; they are why this row is graded medium and not high.
